subtitle: The Dependency Inversion Principle states that an object should depend on high-level modules rather than low-level modules. That sounds a bit complicated. What exactly is a high-level module, and what's a low-level module? The definitions of high/low-level modules are as follows. Substituting this definition into the Dependency Inversion Principle, we can rephrase it as: an object should depend on interfaces rather than on other objects. In other words, this can be interpreted to mean that, as much as possible, inheritance of objects should occur through interfaces.
